newsitem.title: GREECE: EU SEES ALBANIA'S BERISHA AGREEING TO EARLY POLLS.
newsitem.headline: EU SEES ALBANIA'S BERISHA AGREEING TO EARLY POLLS.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha appeared willing to hold early elections to help end a bloody crisis in his Balkan country but had not yet agreed on the timing of the polling, the European Union said on Thursday.
"It is not a matter of if but a matter of when," Dutch Foreign Minister Hans Van Mierlo, whose country currently holds the EU's rotating presidency, told reporters in Athens.
Van Mierlo, who is on an EU mission to help end the crisis in Albania, visited Rome and Athens ahead of flying to Tirana on Friday to meet Berisha and other political leaders.

The first senior Western minister to visit Albania since it imposed emergency rule on Sunday, Van Mierlo said after meeting Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis that the EU was determined to help restore peace to the impoverished country.

Berisha fired the government of Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi on Saturday after weeks of protests sparked by the collapse of pyramid investment schemes exploded into an armed uprising in the south of the country.
Simitis told reporters that Berisha told him in a telephone conversation that he had proposed early elections to Albanian opposition parties but they disagreed on the timing.
Albanian opposition parties want the establishment of a broad-based government before early elections to secure a fair poll.
Van Mierlo said Berisha had agreed to invite an Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) mission, led by former Austrian chancellor Franz Vranitzky, to Albania.
"OSCE is very experienced in monitoring elections," Van Mierlo said. "We believe it can play an important role in holding elections in Albania soon."
In Rome, he made clear that future economic aid from the EU, Albania's biggest source of funds, would depend on a willingness to refrain from violence.

"We want to help but they must make it possible and there should be an underlying agreement between the European Union and Albania on the line to follow," Van Mierlo told a joint news conference with Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini.
Senior Greek diplomats told Reuters that elections would take some time to be held properly and allow a opposition parties to mount a campaign.
"The south is in complete turmoil. It's impossible to have fair elections until some calm is restored there and all political parties have time to organise pre-election campaings," one diplomat said.

After more than five hours of talks with 10 opposition parties on Thursday, Berisha issued a statement offering amnesty to insurgents who turned in their weapons in two days and vowed not to send the Albanian army after them.

It also said Berisha would seek a political consensus on replacing his prime minister but a top Social Democrat, Paskal Milo, said the talks had achieved nothing as Berisha had yet to agree to a coalition government.
